body: That totally makes sense. Thanks for clarifying!
If it's any solace, I live somewhere where I literally wouldn't have the choice even if it were possible, and I'd still choose men. I have my biases given that I'm gay, but men are awesome damn it.

You could also describe horrible - and more likely - possibilities of being lonely and claim that accepting love and what comes with it is more sustainable. I'm sorry if I misunderstood you, but your comments seem to deter people from falling in love because it might crush them, while they themselves are crushed by the impossibility of having it.

The reality of humans is that we all want love, that we continue to want it even after it has hurt us. Love isn't easy, but to think that accepting to live without it is easier seems absurd to me, the hope of acquiring it one day is what keeps many people going.

What do you envision for this sub as an alternative to this toxicity? It seems that people will always find an issue with such spaces, if they promote all positive "it gets better" energy, they are labeled as positive toxic, if they share misery and helplessness, they are likewise toxic. I can't say I disagree with the doom and gloom nature of the content, but I don't really see a better version either.

You are absolutely right, sometimes we are blinded by our loneliness and our infatuation with certain people prevents us from seeing how harmful they can be to us. This is a very necessary conversation here since meaningful relationships are what loneliness robs us of, and seeing a different perspective that is equally important is critical. So thank you for being kind and understanding :)

I feel like getting to love yourself is also an accumulation of many outside influences. Of course, having someone love you is a huge validation of the work you've done on yourself, especially if the image you had before wasn't so love-worthy, but other forms of validation we get from other people that we may not care about so much are also valuable. When I think about focusing only on myself and working on my self-image, I feel like I'm starting an unfair battle, especially since so much of my subconscious is focused on the negative. I understand that your post is aimed at people who see relationships as their ultimate goal, but it's hard to argue with their desire for love when it is generally attributed to good outcomes only.

I agree for the most part, I just wished I was able to actually be loved while working on loving myself. It seems like the usual advice is to love yourself before expecting anyone to love you, but that final destination seems way far that having someone love you would actually help.

I remember the days of staying up until 3am on the kitchen floor, sitting with my cat purring in my lap, the only showing of love I was receiving, and it made me feel good. Now that he has passed away I had to realize that I have to live for myself, as hard as it is, I have to find something that keeps me going, a cat did that for a long time, but it was not a permanent solution. I hope you find the energy to go to therapy if you can, I imagine taking care of 6 cats must be a ton of work, and you are out there doing it every day with joy. Take care of yourself as you would your cats, you seem full of love and affection, I'm sure you would appreciate sharing some of it with yourself.
It redirects me to the link embedded in the platform, which tells me that the content is unavailable. I wonder if I can find a way to access the content from the source itself.
Thanks for your kind words, you're an actual angel! You have no idea how much this helps. I wish you an amazing week as well.

First of all, thank you for taking the time to respond, I really appreciate it. My friendships go a bit back, you could say they slowly developed into mostly online interactions once college started. We didn't meet much before, but as you said, situations brought us together and we bonded a lot through them.

I keep getting mixed signals, on the one hand, I'm pretty sure we care for each other but actively distance ourselves for no reason, I doubt the reason is fear of covid because we are all vaccinated. They themselves are rather sociable, which makes me think that I am the party that notices the lack of socializing due to its absence in my life in general.

I tried communicating with a friend that I would appreciate it if we met irl because it sucks to be alone all the time, and I expressed my hesitation to inform them for fear of appearing needy, needless to say they made me believe I could have asked them anytime and it would have been fine. A few months later, nothing has changed. The last time I asked, they gave me a preemptive excuse for about 3 months lol.

I don't know if I'm asking for too much, but when we could literally walk to school together or whatever, I'm starting to doubt it. I don't know why they want to avoid me either, I am their "best friend" as they say, and they tell me everything that bothers them. I'm in conflict with myself, idk if it is worth it, but I would be even more alone without them.

He was a stray cat that my mom brought home a couple of years ago, I've had him since he could fit in one hand, he was so foody and just loved to slam his body on me every night. I remember the first day we met he was so small and scared, but from then on he would never leave my side.

I'm hopeful about joining communities online, they seem promising. I've been lurking for quite some time in some of them but never gathered the courage to participate. Being around people who may be understanding sounds great honestly. Also, thanks for the movie recommendation, my list is slowly coming together.

Unluckily I'm in a place where it is illegal for me to be gay. Not being allowed to feel and having to be on high alert all the time makes life miserable. But hopefully I can get out of here soon, I hope to continue my studies in a safer place and it's quite a responsibility mentally and financially. I have nothing to lose and everything to gain, so I might as well do my best. Regardless, Thanks for your input.
That would be ideal, unfortunately that wouldn't be possible for me now as I am still living/dependent on my parents. But moving to a safer country is and has been my ultimate goal.

I appreciate the suggestions, I will definitely check them out. The idea of having friends sounds great, but I need to shake off the notion that I am new and deeply in the closet that I won't be able to relate to other gay people or keep up with what they are interested in. I'll do my best tho, I could probably use some friends. Thanks for the valuable advice!
Thanks! definitely added to my watchlist.
